referees.quote: the manuscript requires clearer presentation of the experimental observations and stronger justification for the proposed shear-strain-induced phase stabilization and polaronic behavior.
Overall, this work is well designed and presented. I recommend this manuscript for publication in Nature Communications, given the following questions and suggestions are addressed.

I believe this work merits publication in Nature Communications. However, several issues should be addressed prior to publication. ... additional experimental and theoretical evidence should be provided.

note: The file shows no transfer from another journal; Version 0 is the first round, and no referee co-signs another's report. No referee uses the scale terms, so all levels are inferred. R1 offers no publication verdict and asks for substantial new analysis: refinement details, peak-to-domain mapping, a quantitative shear-strain tensor, temperature-dependent strain and clarification of the polaron mechanism. R2 is borderline: they recommend publication conditionally, but some suggestions (SHG, EELS, thinner TEM lamella) would need new data; these are phrased as questions or optional, hence minor. R3 is borderline: the tone is positive ('merits publication'), but they require additional experimental and theoretical (DFT) evidence and replacement images, hence major. R3 was still not satisfied in round 2.
